main_text.l: non defertur:vel quoniam sensus commu-
nis aliorum omnium princeps & causa præ-
cipua, qui in medio cerebri ventriculo con-
sistit, aut deletus est omninò, aut impedi-
tus. At verò animalis spiritus per epilepsiæ
insultus haud quaquam in cerebro suppri-
mitur aut retinetur, sed uberius in cuncta
membra duci propelliq; videtur, quemad-
modum ex eo motu, quantumuis deprava-
to, qui tum ipsis euenit epilepticis, unicui-
que licet percipere. His adde quòd non
alius est spiritus motui, & alius sensui de-
stinatus, sed unus utriusq; facultatis com-
munis. Quòd igitur epileptici suis paro-
xysmis nihil omninò sentiant, animalem
spiritum causari non oportet, sed sensum
communem (sine quo alij nò sentiunt) qui
tamen non prorsus est deletus, sed dunta-
xat morbo impeditus. Nam si omni ex par-
te deletus esset, profectò non viveret ani-
mal:quandoquidem haud quaquam senti-
ret. At animal, sensu definitur, teste philoso-
pho lib. de Partibus animalium, & earum
causis. Propterea vitæ animalis sensus est
perpetuus comes: sed ob nimiam cerebri
conquassationem, compressionemq;, quæ
epilepticorum paroxysmis fieri contingit,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "quantumuis depravato" (the printed line break after "depraua" shows no hyphen, so the word is written whole); "consistit" (line end "con" with no visible hyphen); "par te" written as "parte" for the same reason. "Quòd" carries the grave accent as printed. "Quod" and "Quòd" are kept as they appear. Printed "s" in the body is written as plain s. The running head is taken as printed. The marginal note "Cap.4.," is shown as printed; its exact punctuation is uncertain.
